sense: a ball, with a bat, a racket or the hand
also: hit the ball out of the park

terms.comment: To push, strike, beat (Cic.): Traupman’s verb for hitting a ball, as pede pulsāre is kicking it (see kick); with the hand, manū pulsāre.
To strike hard, to hit (Cic.); Vives’s verb for hitting the ball at tennis.
Post-Augustan, chiefly of light and sound thrown back (Ov., Verg., Tac.); Lewis & Short cites a discus that rebounds.
Martial’s ball speaks; Varro has pilā expulsim lūdere, play ball hitting it back and forth (Lewis & Short s.v. pila).

evidence: M-O s.v. ball: return (ball), hit back
terms.comment: Morgan–Owens’s verb for returning a ball, after Mercuriale’s repulsus.

phrases.latin: sī mē nōbilibus scīs expulsāre sinistrīs, sum tua. tū nescīs? rūstice, redde pilam
phrases.english: if you can hit me back with a fine left hand, I’m yours. You can’t? Give the ball back, bumpkin!

phrases.latin: Quōmodo ergō percutiunt pilam? pugnō, ut follēs? — Nē sīc quidem, sed rēticulō.
phrases.english: How do they hit the ball, then? With their fist, like footballs? — Not that either: with a racket.
hit the ball out of the park
